articles.title: Turn Spec Drift into a Pull Request Check with SpecGov
articles.excerpt: TL;DR Spec-driven development is useful only while the code and its governing artifacts stay aligned. SpecGov is a local, MIT-licensed CLI and GitHub Action that maps implementation paths to requireme…
articles.body: TL;DR Spec-driven development is useful only while the code and its governing artifacts stay aligned. SpecGov is a local, MIT-licensed CLI and GitHub Action that maps implementation paths to requirements, ADRs, docs, or specs, then reports when a code change bypasses them. This tutorial uses the stable v0.1.0 release to build a small manifest, run a local scan, simulate a pull request check, and add the same check to GitHub Actions. The workflow is advisory first, so a team can learn where its mappings are incomplete before making them blocking. What you will build By the end, a repository will have a .specgov.yml manifest that says which artifacts govern src/auth/** .

articles.title: The Host Networking Stack Is Part of the Guest Isolation Boundary
articles.excerpt: On a KVM host that attaches guests through virtio-net, the host networking stack is part of the guest isolation boundary, whether or not the isolation design drew it that way. CVE-2026-99999, publishe…
articles.body: On a KVM host that attaches guests through virtio-net, the host networking stack is part of the guest isolation boundary, whether or not the isolation design drew it that way. CVE-2026-99999, published on October 15 and fixed upstream in commit 6785011f8b16, is the clearest recent demonstration. A checksum hint supplied by the guest reaches IPv4 code on the host, and that code acts on it after the packet has already been parsed and trusted. The researchers at pwn.ai, who named the flaw PwnEscape, demonstrated host-memory disclosure against Vercel production sandboxes. They also demonstrated host crashes, and they report a host-command-execution chain, on their own KVM and Firecracker machines. The detailed write chain remains unpublished.

CVE-2026-109618 (out-of-memory corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (stale global state after a fatal error). Both are rated CVSS v4.0 9.2 and can allow unauthenticated remote code execution, according to CERT-EU . Who is affected. articles.title: Here is the question I try to ask before I commit to a design: if I'm still on call for this in
articles.excerpt: Here is the question I try to ask before I commit to a design: if I'm still on call for this in three years, and I have to explain it to a new hire on their first week, is this still the right choice?…
articles.body: Here is the question I try to ask before I commit to a design: if I'm still on call for this in three years, and I have to explain it to a new hire on their first week, is this still the right choice? It's a surprisingly strict filter. Clever tricks tend to fail it. The thing that looked elegant on a whiteboard becomes the thing you dread paging through at 2am, and the thing a newcomer can't follow without a ten-minute story about why it's "temporary." Designs that pass tend to be boring in the best way. Fewer moving parts. Names that say what they mean. Behavior you can predict without reading every line. The kind of system where the explanation to the new hire is short, because there isn't much to explain. Most architecture debates are really about the next sprint.

articles.body: Bulkhead is rolling out region locking in multiplayer first-person shooter Wardogs to, in the studio's words, protect "the largest amount of players from an influx of regions that are more prone to cheating." However, legitimate players in Asia have raised concerns, and cross-region players have criticized the developer for blocked from joining their friends. The region lock is done by limiting the maximum ping — the player’s connection with the server — to 175. On paper, this is a fair, non-discriminatory way to stop players from distant regions from entering games with an unstable connection. According to Bulkhead, this would cut down on cheating, too.

articles.body: Capcom has disclosed a data breach of its online membership service affecting over 11 million customer accounts, warning gamers to brace themselves for potential phishing attempts. The Resident Evil, Monster Hunter, and Street Fighter developer said customer information associated with Capcom ID was accessed by a third-party on October 19. 11.7 million email address records were affected globally, exposing date and time of account creation, date and time of last login, number of logins, and the client IP address used during last login. Of these, 43 records of date of birth, gender, country/region, and nickname were affected, and 196 accounts saw unauthorized changes to their Capcom ID login passwords.

articles.title: Faster to Science: A Letter to the Science Community
articles.excerpt: NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall.
articles.body: Dear NASA Science Community, NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall, from NASA Headquarters, to explain our new Competition Model 2.0 (CM 2.0), and answer your questions. We have heard you. We have listened. We know that the burden of bringing great ideas forward has been too heavy for too long. It has taken years to move mission concepts through the current two-step process. This has often come with contract management challenges, unpredictability, and not enough funding. NASA is committed to doing better — and I’m excited to share with you how we’re making it happen.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.) It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year.
